Stated Claim / Post Context:
Ex-boyfriend from hell admits to murdering lover and keeping her severed head in suitcase with a flower inside

Before she was murdered, the woman told a social services worker that if she went missing, it was because her ex-boyfriend killed her.

Actual Article Body:
By ELIOT FORCE, US NEWS REPORTER

Published:  08:35 AEDT, 14 October 2026   |  Updated:  08:47 AEDT, 14 October 2026

A New York man has admitted to murdering his ex-girlfriend, dismembering her body and keeping her severed head in a suitcase along with a flower.

Damon Foy, 50, strangled his ex-girlfriend Alberta Dale, 44, to death sometime between March 31 and April 1 in 2024 soon after she broke things off with him, according to court records reviewed by the Daily Mail.

He then chopped up her body in his home and disposed of everything but her head, which he kept as a kind of sick memento in his apartment in Kerhonkson, a town about 100 miles north of New York City.

Dale had an order of protection against Foy, and the couple had a history of domestic violence. Police began investigating Foy on April 1 after Dale's family reported her missing and requested a welfare check at his apartment.

Officers discovered Dale's severed head in a carry-on suitcase tucked away in Foy's closet on April 2 and arrested him.

He was soon indicted on charges including second-degree murder, aggravated criminal contempt, concealment of a human corpse, criminal contempt, criminal mischief, assault, strangulation and weapons possession.

Foy pleaded guilty to second-degree murder last week. Prosecutors dropped his other charges in exchange for the plea.

Under the agreement, Foy faces 23 years to life in prison, which is two years below the state's maximum sentencing guidelines of 25 to life for second-degree murder. Foy's sentencing hearing is scheduled for December 16.

Alberta Dale, 44, was strangled to death by her ex-boyfriend in 2024. He then chopped up her body and kept her severed head in a suitcase with a flower

Damon Foy, 50, admitted in court last week to murdering Dale. He is now facing 23 years to life in prison and will be sentenced in December

Dale's family reported her missing on April 1 after they had not heard from her for a while and were concerned for the woman's safety, as they were aware of the domestic violence she suffered and the order of protection she had against Foy.

Police conducted two welfare checks at Foy's apartment that day, but did not see Dale. They did note, however, that her car was parked in front of the home.

Foy told officers that Dale had left the home in an Uber or a Lyft a day earlier because she had no money for gas or to fix her car, which is why it was parked out front.

He said that Dale had been at the residence to pick up some of her belongings, but he was not there at the time or when she left because of the order of protection. He added that the last time the two had spoken was over the phone 24 hours earlier.

The next day, a local found a phone on the side of the street and turned it in to police. Detectives quickly determined that it had belonged to Dale.

Around that time, an assistant district attorney also told police that Dale had previously told a staff member at the Ulster County Crime Victims Assistance Program 'that if she went missing, it was because [Foy] killed her.'

Six armed officers returned to Foy's apartment on April 2 and searched the residence with his permission. He had been drinking before they arrived, and he continued to drink and become increasingly intoxicated during the search.

The officers reported a strong smell of bleach in the residence, an open bottle of bleach on the kitchen counter and a pail with a brand-new mop in the corner.

Police found Dale's dismembered remains in Foy's apartment at this complex in Kerhonkson, New York

In one of the two bedrooms on the second floor, the bathroom was 'immaculately clean,' officers observed. An open bag with rubber gloves was inside the master bedroom.

As police searched the residence, Foy told an officer: 'I'm at the point now where I gotta call a lawyer.' He also said: 'I loved this girl.'

Foy was standing in front of a closet, and an officer asked him to move so he could search it. Inside, there was a suitcase that was 'quite heavy for the size of the bag,' police noted.

When a deputy shined a flashlight on the suitcase, he saw what appeared to be dried blood on it. When asked what it was, Foy got defensive, held up his hands and said: 'See, no defensive wounds.'

A detective asked Foy if Dale was in the suitcase, to which he replied: 'Are you out of your mind?'

The officers then remained in the residence while waiting for a warrant to search the suitcase. During the wait, Foy whispered to one of the detectives: 'I killed her. She's in there, I killed her.'

Once police received the warrant and opened the suitcase, they found Dale's severed head, but the rest of her remains were missing. A flower was also inside.

When a detective interviewed Foy in custody the next day, he asked why Foy had placed the flower in the bag.

The murderer said, 'I loved that girl' and that he was trying to figure out 'what still happened last night to take s*** over the top.'
